title: Great news Idea guys,this is a perfect time to be alive!
author: Due-Huckleberry-2222
selftext:
To all the “ideas guys” out there: this is 100% the time to be alive.Yeah — that distinction is the heart of the post. The AI prototype is not the product. It’s the cheapest, fastest way to answer: “Will actual players enjoy this idea?” And somebody refusing it on principle because AI touched it isn’t testing the game.

To all the “ideas guys” out there: this is 100% the time to be alive.

If you've spent years saying, “I've got this game idea, but I don't know how to build it,” your world just changed.

You have AI now.

Build the damn thing.

Not the final game.

Not the Steam release.

Not the beautifully coded version you're going to sell.

Build a TEST.

Use AI to make the ugliest, simplest playable version of your idea you can. Put it on a website. Send people a link. Get it in front of actual players and see what happens.

And I want to emphasize this because I see it constantly:

THE TROLLS ARE COMING.

The second you mention AI, somebody on Reddit is going to say:

"AI garbage."

"Nobody is going to play this."

"I would never play an AI game."

"Learn to code."

Whatever.

Those aren't your players. Those are Reddit commenters reacting to AI.

Don't let them burn you out.

Because you're not asking whether somebody wants to buy an AI-generated game.

THAT ISN'T THE POINT.

You're using AI to build a prototype so actual human beings can try your game idea.

That's it.

Think of it like cardboard, index cards, dice, placeholder art, or a paper prototype.

Nobody looks at a cardboard prototype and screams:

"NOBODY IS GOING TO BUY A GAME MADE OUT OF INDEX CARDS!"

Of course they're not.

It's a prototype.

AI lets somebody with an idea make the digital equivalent ridiculously fast.

You're trying to answer one question:

IS THIS FUN?

Do people click?

Do they understand it?

Do they finish a game?

Do they play another round?

Do they send it to somebody?

Do they ask when you're adding more?

That's player feedback.

Someone commenting “AI sucks and nobody will play this” without ever playing your game isn't player feedback.

Don't confuse the two.

And here's the other uncomfortable truth:

Games are a dime a dozen. Ideas are a dime a dozen.

Your completely original game idea probably isn't quite as original as you think.

The hardest part isn't coming up with the idea.

THE HARDEST PART IS GETTING PLAYERS.

So learn that part now.

Don't spend two years building something and THEN discover nobody cares.

Build the crappy AI prototype this weekend.

Put it online.

Try to get 10 people to play it.

Then 50.

Then 100.

And if nobody plays it?

Awesome.

You just learned that for almost nothing.

Change it. Try another idea. Try another audience.

But what happens if people actually start playing?

Now you can come back to Reddit and instead of saying:

"I have an amazing game idea. Will somebody help me build it?"

You can say:

"I built a prototype. 300 people tried it. 80 played more than once. Here's what they liked. Now I need a real developer/artist/designer to help me build the actual game."

THAT is a completely different conversation.

Now you're not asking strangers to believe your idea is good.

You've got evidence.

And people are a hell of a lot more interested in joining something when there's evidence that somebody actually wants it.

That's why this is such an incredible time to be an ideas person.

AI doesn't mean you don't need developers.

It doesn't mean you don't need artists.

It doesn't mean you don't need designers.

If the idea works, you'll probably need all of them.

AI simply lets you answer the question that used to cost a fortune:

“IS THIS WORTH BUILDING?”

So don't let somebody shame you out of testing your idea because your prototype used AI.

You're not building the final product.

You're building something people can TRY.

Build the ugly version.

Find actual players.

Watch what they do.

Listen to them.

Then decide whether it's worth building the real thing.

AI didn't make ideas more valuable.

It made proving ideas cheaper.

And if you've spent your whole life with a notebook full of game ideas?

This is your moment.!

P.S. — And yes, before the trolls arrive:

This post was not written by AI. I wrote it.

AI cleaned it up, fixed my grammar, organized my thoughts, and made it easier to read.

You know… exactly the kind of thing I'm talking about in this post.

I had the idea. I had the opinion. I had something I wanted to say.

I used a tool to help me present it better.

So you can save the “LOL, this was obviously written by AI” comment.

Edited by AI? Absolutely.

Thought up by AI? Nope.

There's a difference.

And that difference is pretty much the entire point.

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: Can0pen3r
comments.body: It apparently didn't do a particularly good job of cleaning up, organizing, or making your thoughts easier to read. Especially considering that basically the entire intended body of the post is there twice, back to back...

replies.author: Due-Huckleberry-2222
replies.body: And just like that my point is made thanks

replies.author: Can0pen3r
replies.body:
Your point was that you're glazing LLMs as being more capable and efficient than they actually are? All I did was point out the entirely legitimate observation that it didn't actually do as good of a job as you were giving it credit for. The passive aggressively defensive bit is not only unnecessary, it's just silly and makes your point feel less valid.

Regardless of my personal feelings on the matter, AI is genuinely capable of some pretty impressive stuff. However, it's not some magic silver bullet that does everything right, and acting like anyone that recognizes that it isn't perfect is somehow actively bashing it (or you) is just going to hurt your case.

Lol

replies.author: Can0pen3r
replies.body:
I actually did, that's how I knew that the first 90% had been repeated before you went back and changed it (not condemning, that's how editing and iteration are supposed to work and it's the whole reason that posts are editable in the first place. Ironically I read it all the way through with an open mind.

That's why my initial comment was directly addressing the statement made at the very end and it wasn't hateful or meant as a jab at you or at AI. It was literally just a factual observation that the AI didn't do as good of a job at organizing the post as you seemed to think because it had duplicated 90% of the post so that it got almost all the way to the end of the intended body of text and then started over with the exact same thing, verbatim...

Again, that's not a slight against you or the program. It's just a factual observation. I don't understand the need to read more into it than it actually is, like I'm making some kind of a direct attack on you when all I did was address an error in the post (an error which you promptly fixed and should've been the end of this pointless conversation.) If anything it kinda seems like you're not actually reading the comments and just interpreting them as attacks and reacting without actually reading what's being said...
